title: Personal Positions, Evidence, and Ethical Boundaries
status: De-identified edition; no new personal claims

scope.purpose: Provide a readable and structured account of declared ethical positions and their relationships.
scope.source_boundary: The supplied doctrine statements and the associated conversation, approvals, dossier, and consistency review.
scope.method: Combine the two dossier parts, apply the accepted review corrections, paraphrase distinctive wording, and retain evidential distinctions.
scope.identity_policy: Use no personal name, account, source locator, precise date, or persistent person identifier. Record and source IDs are local to this document.
scope.authority: Production of this edition was explicitly approved. This record does not itself authorize external publication, transfer, prediction, imitation, authentication, or delegation.
scope.limit: The account describes declared positions, not a complete person, independently verified conduct, or a unique cognitive method.

anonymization.classification: De-identified; irreversible anonymity is not established.
removed: Repository addresses and local file paths
Attachment, chat, and other identity-bearing identifiers
Sensitive personal context not necessary to express the ethical position
retained: Differences between declarations and editorial interpretations
anonymization.residual_risk: A reader familiar with the source may recognize the combination of ideas. De-identification reduces direct identification and does not guarantee that recognition is impossible.

evidence_classes.description: A position expressed directly by the individual in the source conversation.
A position contained in supplied text; inclusion does not independently establish authorship of every sentence.
Wording or organization produced by the assistant.
Approval of a described activity or interpretation, limited to its stated scope.
A relationship or explanation drawn from sources and kept distinct from a direct declaration.
A question for which the record does not establish a responsible conclusion.

sources.description: Initial doctrine distinguishing examination of intellectual work from attributable personal profiling.
Clarification that explicit permission can permit the relevant profiling or archival activity.
Approved earlier expansion incorporating the permission condition.
Later extended doctrine covering evidence, operational use, adaptation, correction, and limits on personal interpretation.
Statement introducing coincidental approximation, delayed recognition, removal of unauthorized influence, and voluntary mediation.
Approved interpretation of approximation, correction, and mediation, subsequently developed as a companion statement.
Bounded approvals for the dossier and its analytical continuation.
Consistency review accepted before authorization of the de-identified edition.

records.statement: Permission to examine intellectual work does not automatically include permission to create an attributable profile of its creator.
limitations: Does not automatically classify every instance of pattern recognition as personal profiling.

records.statement: Explicit permission may authorize a defined activity; a material expansion requires renewed permission.
records.interpretive_status: Direct clarification developed in subsequent documents.
limitations: Does not establish permission beyond the activity actually approved.

records.statement: Crediting a contribution and obtaining permission serve different obligations; neither automatically substitutes for the other.
limitations: Does not determine ownership or dependence in an individual dispute.

records.statement: Statements, observations, inferences, corroboration, and attestations must remain distinguishable, with claims limited to what their evidence establishes.
limitations: Classification alone does not make a claim accurate or verified.

records.statement: A retained account of a person does not acquire authority to override that person's present instruction or correction.
limitations: Does not resolve every conflict involving identity, context, prior constraints, or third-party interests.

records.statement: Similar expression can result from shared conventions, task constraints, or coincidence; resemblance alone does not settle derivation.
records.interpretive_status: Direct position with an approved qualification: the relevant construction set is task-constrained, not a claim that language has only finitely many possible expressions.
limitations: No probability of coincidence is established.
A claim of coincidence does not establish independence.

records.statement: An instruction excluding material establishes a boundary but does not independently prove that a resulting output has no dependence on that material.
records.interpretive_status: Approved interpretation of the distinction between a restriction and demonstrated compliance.
limitations: Does not establish that a particular system accessed a particular source.
The meaning of restricted implementation material depends on the governing context.

records.statement: The individual affirms an ethical commitment while acknowledging that sustained interest may precede recognition of a boundary crossing.
records.interpretive_status: Generalized declaration preserving commitment and delayed recognition while omitting sensitive personal context.
limitations: Does not establish perfect conduct, absence of responsibility, or an independent explanation of behavior.

records.statement: When unauthorized reliance is identified, the response should include stopping that reliance and addressing affected work within the available authority.
records.interpretive_status: Approved interpretation of removal and redress.
limitations: Suspected influence, known dependence, and established unauthorized use remain different statuses.
A declaration of removal does not establish complete removal.
Does not authorize destruction of records or changes to another person's work.

records.statement: Non-coercive transfers should remain open to voluntary clarification, negotiation, and remedy.
records.interpretive_status: Approved interpretation of the individual's commitment to mediation.
limitations: Does not guarantee participation, agreement, ownership, transfer authority, or legal effectiveness.
Later agreement does not establish that earlier permission existed.

records.statement: Personal interpretation should avoid turning metaphor, favorable description, or speculative language into unsupported claims about essential identity.
records.interpretive_status: Supported limit on inflated personal interpretation.
limitations: Does not prohibit clearly identified imaginative representation or praise.

records.statement: Corrections and competing accounts should retain enough provenance to explain their treatment, subject to permission and confidentiality.
limitations: Does not authorize unrestricted retention of protected material.
No universal retention period or procedure is established.

records.statement: The record supports declared standards and a history of their development more strongly than it supports findings about conduct outside the record.
limitations: Does not infer compliance or noncompliance from the absence of independent evidence.

records.statement: Approving production, receiving an artifact, reviewing it, and accepting its contents are distinct events.
records.interpretive_status: Supported distinction applied to the dossier and its review.
limitations: Acceptance of a review does not establish independent verification of all personal claims.
No universal rule of precedence among document versions has been established.

development.description: The source distinguished study of work from personal reconstruction.
Permission was clarified as capable of authorizing bounded activity.
The account expanded to evidence handling, adaptive systems, correction, and personal authority.
Coincidence, delayed recognition, removal of unauthorized reliance, and mediation received separate treatment.
A bounded dossier and continuation were produced. A consistency review was accepted before this de-identified edition was authorized.

relationships.title: Commitment and recognition
relationships.interpretation: A continuing ethical commitment can be recorded alongside delayed recognition. The authorization, event, awareness, and response still require separate assessment.
relationships.limitation: No general threshold for responsibility or adequate remedy is established.

relationships.title: Convergence and dependence
relationships.interpretation: Possible convergence limits unsupported accusations, while known dependence still requires honest treatment.
relationships.limitation: Neither resemblance nor a claim of coincidence resolves a particular case alone.

relationships.title: Removal and correction history
relationships.interpretation: Stopping reliance and retaining an accountable correction record may serve different purposes and require distinct permissions.
relationships.limitation: The need for accountability does not authorize duplication of restricted material.

relationships.title: Permission and mediation
relationships.interpretation: A later agreement may set future terms or address an earlier dispute without establishing that permission existed earlier.
relationships.limitation: Agreement about future use need not settle all historical claims.

relationships.title: Adaptation and authority
relationships.interpretation: A personal account may assist communication while remaining subordinate to explicit instructions and the limits of its authorization.
relationships.limitation: It cannot grant itself authority to act for the person.

hypothetical_cases.title: Recognition after a change in analytical purpose
hypothetical_cases.scenario: A reviewer permitted to examine a work begins constructing a creator profile and later notices that profiling was excluded.
hypothetical_cases.assessment: Stop and assess the affected activity. Delayed recognition does not determine whether the earlier activity was authorized or what remedy is sufficient.
hypothetical_cases.unresolved: The timing of awareness and the proportionate remedy require case-specific evidence.

hypothetical_cases.title: Resemblance after source exclusion
hypothetical_cases.scenario: An output resembles a short construction in material that was excluded from the task.
hypothetical_cases.assessment: Record the resemblance and restriction separately. Examine competing explanations without treating either coincidence or a violation as established.
hypothetical_cases.unresolved: The available evidence may not resolve derivation.

hypothetical_cases.title: Replacement with a correction record
hypothetical_cases.scenario: An author replaces an identified unauthorized contribution and keeps a bounded explanation of the correction.
hypothetical_cases.assessment: Assess permission for the replacement and the correction record separately. Do not claim universal removal without support.
hypothetical_cases.unresolved: Retention, access, and any claim of replacement independence remain context-dependent.

hypothetical_cases.title: Disputed voluntary transfer
hypothetical_cases.scenario: Two parties agree an exchange was voluntary but disagree about the uses it permitted.
hypothetical_cases.assessment: Clarify the disputed scope and consider future agreement without rewriting the chronology of permission.
hypothetical_cases.unresolved: Participation, settlement terms, and authority to agree have not been established.

hypothetical_cases.title: An inferred preference conflicts with a request
hypothetical_cases.scenario: A system expects a detailed response, but the individual requests brevity.
hypothetical_cases.assessment: The inferred preference does not independently authorize overriding the current request. Expose material ambiguity rather than resolving it invisibly through a profile.
hypothetical_cases.unresolved: More consequential conflicts may require clarification of identity, context, or prior explicit constraints.

unresolved_questions.question: Which formulation governs when document versions differ?
What do restricted implementation terms mean in a particular authorized activity?
What evidence is sufficient to classify a resemblance as independent, influenced, dependent, or unresolved?
When should a disputed output remain qualified, be isolated, or be withdrawn?
What establishes sufficient removal when influence cannot be separated reliably?
What minimum correction record is necessary and permitted?
How should delayed recognition, negligent disregard, and deliberate circumvention be distinguished?
What voluntary mediation process and completion conditions would the parties accept?
What future uses of the dossier, if any, will be separately authorized?

review_checklist: Check whether each statement accurately represents the intended position.
Check whether source material and editorial wording remain distinguishable.
Identify any statement generalized beyond its original context.
Identify omitted qualifications or added implications.
Confirm that hypothetical examples are not mistaken for personal history.
Clarify terminology where its meaning affects permission or remedy.
Identify any material requiring further restriction.
Distinguish correction of an editorial error from a changed position.
Record acceptance explicitly rather than inferring it from silence.

review_status.consistency_review: The preceding review was accepted and its corrections are incorporated in this edition.
review_status.edition_content_acceptance: Not yet recorded after delivery of this edition.
review_status.independent_verification: No independent verification of personal claims or conduct is asserted.
review_status.further_use: Machine-readable preparation is authorized. This file does not independently authorize external ingestion, sharing, or operational personal modeling.
